headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from Flowise’s shared server datastore and filesystem, while Superset’s limited API surface reduces direct conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write files and uses browser/API tools in flows; its shared state is via server datastore. Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. If Flowise outputs attacker-controlled content into shared files or datastore, Superset-side automation could ingest it as trusted input. The pathway is plausible in default deployments, though not proven.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled content into shared datastore or files that Superset later reads
IF Superset automation treats Flowise-produced content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared writable folders between the agents
Add provenance tags to all Flowise outputs before Superset consumes them
Require manual review for any Flowise-generated text before API execution
Separate runtime accounts and storage paths
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and secrets, and has broad network egress. Superset has allowlisted egress and a Superset API. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive Flowise inputs can flow into Superset outputs or API calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files
IF Superset API calls include content derived from Flowise chatflow inputs or outputs
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories
Restrict Flowise secrets to a dedicated vault
Review Superset API payloads for embedded sensitive text
Turn off cross-agent file sharing by default
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the filesystem and run browser-based tools, while Superset exposes only a Superset API and allowlisted egress. There is no evidence that both agents write the same mutable resource or share locks, so direct write-write conflict is not established. The main overlap is limited and the blast radius appears small without a shared writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or database
IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same mutable API credentials
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Use distinct output directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources
Add file-locking around any shared artifact
requires-engineering: introduce resource-level locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and Superset exposes APIs that could act on those outputs. If Superset treats Flowise-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade from generation to downstream actions. Because the profiles do not document verification gates between them, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Superset consumes Flowise output without validation
IF Flowise-generated facts are used to populate dashboards, queries, or API actions
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Superset consumes Flowise output
Require citations or source links for generated claims
Limit Flowise outputs to drafts only
Log and review any downstream API action triggered by Flowise text
requires-engineering: add schema validation between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Flowise explicitly handles model provider keys, tool credentials, and chatflow inputs/outputs, while Superset’s touched data classes are unspecified. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Flowise chatflows
IF Superset stores or exports the same regulated data class under a different retention policy
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Document retention settings for both agents
Review secret-handling paths in Flowise
Confirm Superset export/delete behavior before use
requires-engineering: align data-governance policies across both systems
